# 8-Week Weight Loss Training Plan Overview

## Plan Strategy
This 8-week progressive training plan is designed to support sustainable weight loss while building lean muscle and improving cardiovascular fitness. With 4 training days per week and no equipment required, the plan leverages bodyweight exercises, running, and interval training to create a caloric deficit while preserving muscle mass.

## Profile Analysis
At age 30 with intermediate fitness level and 1 year of training history, you have a solid foundation to progress into higher-intensity work. Your 75kg bodyweight at 175cm (BMI ~24.5) indicates a relatively healthy starting point, making this an ideal time to focus on body composition changes through strategic training combined with nutrition.

## Training Structure
Each week consists of 4 training days organized as:
- **2 Strength Sessions**: Bodyweight resistance training targeting major muscle groups
- **1-2 Cardio/Interval Sessions**: Mixed steady-state and high-intensity interval training (HIIT)
- **Active Recovery/Flexibility**: Integrated into training days or separate

This structure maintains metabolic demand, preserves muscle mass during weight loss, and improves cardiovascular health.

## Phase Breakdown

### Phase 1: Base Building & Adaptation (Weeks 1-3)
Focus on establishing consistent training habits, learning proper movement patterns, and building aerobic capacity. Volume is moderate with controlled intensity increases.

### Phase 2: Build & Intensification (Weeks 4-6)
Progressive increase in training intensity through higher-intensity interval work, increased repetitions, and longer cardio sessions. This phase maximizes caloric burn while maintaining muscle.

### Phase 3: Peak Maintenance & Consolidation (Weeks 7-8)
Maintain intensity while strategically managing volume to prevent overtraining. Focus shifts to consistency and sustainable habits for continued progress beyond 8 weeks.

## Expected Outcomes
Following this plan with proper nutrition, expect:
- 2-3 kg weight loss (primarily fat with muscle retention)
- Improved cardiovascular fitness and endurance
- Increased muscular endurance and body control
- Better metabolic conditioning and work capacity

## Key Considerations
- Progressive overload through volume increases, intensity progression, and exercise complexity
- No equipment required—all exercises use bodyweight or minimal external tools
- Recovery is emphasized through adequate rest days and proper warm-up/cool-down
- Nutrition and sleep are critical; training alone cannot achieve weight loss goals
- Flexibility and mobility work should be incorporated 2-3x per week

## Timeline to Goal
With target date of June 14, 2026 (91 days), this 8-week plan represents the critical foundation period. Additional training phases beyond week 8 can be programmed for continued progression toward the goal date.

phase_breakdown.description: Establish training consistency and movement competency. Week 1-2 emphasize steady-state cardio (3-4km runs or equivalent) 2x weekly and 2 full-body strength sessions with moderate volume. Week 3 introduces first interval work with 1 HIIT session. All exercises use bodyweight (push-ups, squats, lunges, planks, burpees). Focus on proper form and building work capacity. Total training volume ~8-10 hours.

Increase training demand through higher-intensity interval training and strength volume. Shift to 2 structured strength sessions with progressive overload (increased reps/sets, reduced rest periods, exercise variations). Add 2 dedicated cardio sessions including 1 HIIT day and 1 moderate-intensity run. Introduce circuit training combining strength and conditioning. Rep ranges shift to 12-15 for muscular endurance. Total training volume ~10-12 hours with higher intensity.

Consolidate gains while managing fatigue. Maintain intensity but reduce excessive volume to prevent overtraining. 2 strength sessions remain challenging but focus on quality and muscle tension. 2 cardio sessions balance HIIT (1x) and steady-state (1x). Emphasize consistency, recovery practices, and establishing long-term sustainable training habits. Prepare mentally and physically for continued progression beyond 8 weeks. Total training volume ~9-11 hours with maintained intensity.
